clue.text: Computer showing picture of one's mother?

definitions.text: Computer showing picture of one's mother?

parts.words: Computer showing picture of one's mother?
parts.note: a framed photo of mum puts mum inside a border, and the big central computer's name can be split to say just that

explanation.surface: Someone's computer screen displays a photo of their mum.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as MA / IN / FRAME: a picture of one's mother is Ma in a frame. The question mark flags the whimsical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A large central computer serving many terminals is called by this name.

clue.text: Letters from American composer's daughter?

parts.note: an unmarried daughter is addressed by the title Miss
Charles Ives was a modernist American composer

explanation.surface: Correspondence written by the daughter of a US composer.
explanation.walkthrough: The composer's daughter would be called Miss, then his surname, Ives; the pieces are written in that order even though the clue names the composer first.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal written messages sent to someone are known by this word.

clue.text: Artist made an entrance, privately seeing judge

parts.note: 'in came' is a way of saying someone entered
RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: An artist walks in to see a judge in private.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Artist made an entrance' as 'In came RA'. A case heard in camera is heard privately, in the judge's chambers rather than open court.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin legal phrase for hearings held away from the public, in chambers.

clue.text: Preserved in a way, mostly from eastern religion

indicators.note: only most of the word from is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: Zen is a school of Buddhism from Japan and China

explanation.surface: Something kept intact by some method that comes chiefly from an Eastern faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the last letter off 'from', leaving FRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilling food solid in a freezer is one method of keeping it.

clue.text: On edge about university's central hall

indicators.note: the phrase for on edge goes around the letter for university

parts.note: on the edge is 'at rim'
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A nervous person is uneasy about the university's main hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On edge' looks like nervousness but is AT RIM; 'about' puts it around U.
explanation.definitionFit: An open central court or lofty entrance space in a building has this Latin name.

clue.text: Blessed with prospect of success, following wise plan, finally

indicators.note: following means the phrase for success comes after those closing letters
finally takes the closing letter of each of the two words wise and plan

parts.note: a plan likely to work is viable

explanation.surface: A fortunate person, likely to succeed after a sensible plan is finally carried out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letters of 'wise' and 'plan', E and N; 'following' puts VIABLE after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being blessed with good things makes one's position one that others covet.

clue.text: Delicate female bird

parts.note: the rail is a marsh bird, as in the water rail

explanation.surface: A fragile hen bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something weak and easily broken.

clue.text: She takes one side in argument, if it's involved with men

definitions.text: She takes one side in argument

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman picks a side in a debate because men are mixed up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges IF IT'S and MEN; 'with' only joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaigner for women's rights is cast as a woman taking a side in the gender debate.

clue.text: Having an inclination, did some fishing

definitions.meaning: went fishing with rod and line

explanation.surface: Someone keen on it went fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both set at a slope and fished with a hook and line.

clue.text: Caseworker wrapping wife in sheet

indicators.note: in places the wife's letter inside the word for a sheet

parts.note: a sheet is a layer, as of material

explanation.surface: A social worker wraps his wife up in a bed sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caseworker' suggests social work, but it means someone who handles legal cases.
explanation.definitionFit: A solicitor or barrister works on legal cases for clients.

clue.text: Support during hardship victim of trickery articulated

indicators.note: articulated means spoken aloud, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: a sucker is someone easily fooled

explanation.surface: A victim of a con speaks up asking for help in hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: Help and relief given in times of distress is this old word.

clue.text: At the outset, as laser, for example, was constructed?

definitions.text: as laser, for example, was constructed?
definitions.meaning: laser was built from the first letters of light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation

explanation.surface: How a laser was first built.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means at first and also formed from the first letters of words, like an acronym.

clue.text: Enthusiasm about volcano in eastern country

indicators.note: about means the word for enthusiasm wraps around the volcano

parts.note: vim means energy or zest
Etna is the volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: Keenness about a volcano in an Eastern land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the volcano inside the enthusiasm word, after its second letter; 'in' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation in South-East Asia, east from a European standpoint.

clue.text: Not seeing leading lady in great performance

parts.note: unable to see is blind
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, first lady of the land

explanation.surface: A sightless leading actress gives a superb performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading lady' suggests an actress, but it is the Queen, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for an outstanding display, especially in sport.

clue.text: Courses with coach providing guidance for players

parts.note: a stagecoach, or stage, is a horse-drawn coach
courses are routes or directions taken

explanation.surface: Training sessions with a coach give advice to sports players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' and 'coach' suggest sport, but the players are actors and the coach is a stagecoach.
explanation.definitionFit: Instructions in a script tell actors where to move and how to act.

clue.text: Representative sent from corrupt emirs, say

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An envoy dispatched by crooked Gulf rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges EMIRS and SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy sent on a mission on someone's behalf.

clue.text: Highly enjoyable kind of movie

parts.note: a film enjoyed literally high up, watched by passengers on a plane journey

explanation.surface: A really fun sort of film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly' is literal: the film is shown up in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Films shown to airline passengers during a journey get this label.

clue.text: Bring about a special event

explanation.surface: Arrange a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to cause; as a noun, a notable function or event.

clue.text: Pastor — one wearing dog-collar if German

definitions.meaning: a minister caring for a flock of believers
the German breed of dog wears a collar

explanation.surface: A clergyman wearing a clerical collar is German.
explanation.walkthrough: The dog-collar suggests a clergyman's collar, but it is also a real dog's: the German breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is literally one who tends a flock, and the word also names a herder of sheep, as in the German dog breed.

clue.text: Dog finding a body on motorway

indicators.note: on means the phrase a body sits upon the motorway letter, so it is written after it

parts.note: M stands for motorway, as in the M1
a stiff is slang for a corpse

explanation.surface: A dog finds a corpse on the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A large powerful breed of guard dog.

clue.text: Humble, in two ways

parts.note: a mode is a way of doing something
ST, street, is a way or road

explanation.surface: Being humble in two senses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two ways' gives two different words for way: MODE and ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Unassuming and not boastful.

clue.text: Make no noise, being imprisoned

explanation.surface: Keep quiet while locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: As an order it means be quiet; it also means confined behind bars.

clue.text: E.g. Oil or water, for car or bus

definitions.meaning: oil or water as the liquid medium carrying a pigment or drug
a means of transport on the road

explanation.surface: Oil or water as fuel for cars and buses.
explanation.walkthrough: In painting and medicine the liquid in which pigment or a drug is carried is called by this word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a carrying medium and a conveyance for transport.

clue.text: A raider from sea, as opposed to one ruler over land

parts.note: V is short for versus, against
I is the Roman numeral one
a king rules a country

explanation.surface: A sea raider set against a monarch ruling on land.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse seafarers who raided coasts of Europe.

clue.text: Within truth one stays, being this

definitions.text: Within truth one stays, being this

indicators.note: within points to letters found running inside the words truth one stays

explanation.surface: Someone who always keeps to the truth is described this way.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is lodged inside 'truth one stays', and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A truthful person stays within the truth.

clue.text: Something percussionist needs for low joint in turkey, say?

definitions.meaning: the stick used to beat a drum
the lower part of a poultry leg

explanation.surface: A drummer needs a turkey leg for something.
explanation.definitionFit: One word for a drummer's beater and for the lower leg of a cooked fowl.

clue.text: Put in list that is including letters in times

indicators.note: including means the abbreviation for that is holds the rearranged letters

parts.note: i.e., id est, means that is

indicators.note: the letters in the word times are taken and reordered

explanation.surface: Listing items in a newspaper's columns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters in' asks for the letters of 'times' in a new order, and 'including' sets them inside the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out item by item, as in a bill.

clue.text: Drunk getting extremely silly after gratuitous advice?

indicators.note: after places the edge letters behind the word for advice

parts.note: a tip is advice given for free, and also a gratuity

indicators.note: extremely takes the first and last letters of the word silly

explanation.surface: A drunk becomes very foolish after being given free advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely silly' gives S and Y, the first and last letters of 'silly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly drunk, merry from alcohol.

clue.text: Get in the wrong dinghy, initially, that's securely fastened

indicators.note: wrong means badly done, so these letters are rearranged
initially takes the opening letter of the word dinghy

explanation.surface: Climbing into the wrong boat, which is tied up securely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges GET IN THE, then the first letter of 'dinghy' is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Made tight or firm, as with a knot or a screw.
